subproblem.title: Integrability of a continuous radial profile g(|x - y|/t) that vanishes beyond T
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, E := R^{n+l} (Euclidean space), mu a measure on E, y in E, g : R -> R and S, T, t real numbers. Write B_S(y) for the closed ball of radius S about y. Assume: mu(B_S(y)) < infinity; g is continuous; g(u) = 0 for every u > T; t > 0; and T t < S. Then the real function x -> g(|x - y|/t) is mu-integrable on E.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (y : Amb n ℓ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (S T t : ℝ), μ (closedBall y S) < ⊤ → Continuous g → (∀ u : ℝ, T < u → g u = 0) → 0 < t → T * t < S → Integrable (fun x => g (‖x - y‖ / t)) μ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1(c), 2 and 3 of the supplied proof of ted_lpm_fcm_cutoff_mass_hasDerivAt (the integrability parts (a) and (b)), stated for an arbitrary continuous radial profile g. Part (a) is the case g = phi; part (b) is the case g(u) = u phi'(u).

Notation: B := B_S(y) the closed ball, h(x) := g(|x - y|/t).

1. A bound for g on [0, infinity). g is continuous, hence bounded on the compact interval [0, T], which is empty if T < 0 (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). So there is K0 with |g(u)| <= K0 for all u in [0, T]. Put K := max(K0, 0).
 - If 0 <= u <= T, then |g(u)| <= K0 <= K.
 - If u > T, then g(u) = 0 by hypothesis, so |g(u)| = 0 <= K.
 Hence |g(u)| <= K for every u >= 0.

2. Measurability. h is continuous on E, as the composition of the continuous maps x -> |x - y|, division by the constant t, and g. A continuous real function on E is a.e. strongly measurable for every measure (E carries its Borel sigma-algebra), in particular for mu restricted to B.

3. Uniform bound. For every x in E, |x - y|/t >= 0 because t > 0. So |h(x)| <= K by step 1.

4. Integrability on B. B has finite mu-measure by hypothesis. By steps 2 and 3, h is a.e. strongly measurable for mu restricted to B and bounded by K there. Hence h is integrable on B (IntegrableOn.of_bound).

5. Vanishing off B. Let x lie outside B. Then |x - y| > S, and S > T t by hypothesis, so |x - y| > T t. Dividing by t > 0 gives |x - y|/t > T, hence h(x) = g(|x - y|/t) = 0.

6. Conclusion. h is integrable on B and vanishes at every point outside B, so h is mu-integrable (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero).
proof_key_steps: |g(u)| <= K for all u >= 0, by compactness of [0, T] and g = 0 on (T, infinity).
x -> g(|x - y|/t) is continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable, and it is bounded by K everywhere because |x - y|/t >= 0.
It is integrable on B_S(y), which has finite mu-measure (IntegrableOn.of_bound).
It vanishes outside B_S(y), because there |x - y| > S > T t gives |x - y|/t > T.
Being integrable on B_S(y) and zero outside it, the function is mu-integrable (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero).

audit.reason: The prose and independent one-line Lean proposition match, including the absence of T > 0. The compact-interval argument with K = max(K0, 0) remains valid when T < 0. Continuity supplies measurability; the uniform bound and finite ball measure give integrability on the ball; T*t < S and t > 0 give vanishing outside it. These steps prove the exact statement without circularity or deferred proof construction. The bare name is unreserved. Applying it to φ and u ↦ u*deriv φ u establishes parent conclusions (a) and (b).
